$comment: Project-wide tracker configuration. Layer 2 of four: built-in defaults (tools/tracker/config.mjs) <- THIS FILE <- .tracker/hosts/<hostname>.json <- AEMDEV_QA_* env. A host profile may tune transport (endpoints, models, timeouts, token caps) and host.role only; anything that changes the evidence a judge sees — qa.maxTextWords, qa.wordRatio — belongs HERE, for every host, because a verdict that depends on which machine ran it is worthless. The locale list is deliberately absent: it is imported from scripts/tracker/locales.js so the pipeline and the browser cannot disagree, and an override here would replace it wholesale (deepMerge replaces arrays) with no error.

llm.$comment: Three local llama.cpp servers, one per tier. Confirmed running on host fw13-ubuntu at these ports. A machine serving them elsewhere sets its own endpoints in .tracker/hosts/<hostname>.json rather than editing this file.

publish.$comment: One DA site holds both the content and the tracker. `branch` is the ref every surface derives from — the aem.page host the drivers judge against and the Preview link written into every review doc — so a feature branch here would send reviewers to a host that disappears when someone deletes the branch. Use --branch=<ref> for the rare page that must be checked against unlanded code.

qa.$comment: Verdict-affecting thresholds; host profiles must not override these. Values are inherited from the pipeline this was ported from and have NOT been recalibrated on aemdev pages — recalibration belongs in .tracker/qa-baselines/<group>.json, because a tolerance is a property of a template, not of a machine.
qa.$comment-minConfidence: The judge's confidence gate: a model `pass` below this escalates instead (tools/tracker/judge.mjs, merge ladder step 4). It lives HERE and not in a host profile for the reason above — it decides verdicts. The upstream pipeline declared confidence in its schema, promised this gate in a header comment, implemented none of it, and emitted `95` against a 0..1 schema for months because llama.cpp's strict mode enforces types and not ranges. 0.55 is deliberately low: it is a floor against a model that has already told you it is guessing, not a quality bar, and every page it catches goes to a human rather than to a recorded PASS.

tx.$comment: The translation lifecycle's observe-and-dispatch half: tx:scan, tx:send, tx:preview. `requestsPerSecond` is a ceiling on admin.hlx.page, which rate-limits at about 10/s — a concurrency cap alone does NOT bound the rate, because the status API answers in ~80ms and six lanes against it is well over 60/s. The two SLA windows turn the one unobservable state into something falsifiable: a pair recorded `sent` whose page has not appeared on the preview host after previewSlaHours becomes `preview-missing` (queue awaiting-preview), and a signed-off page that never reached the live host after publishSlaHours becomes `publish-fail`. Both are deliberately generous — DA's Translate app is driven by a human opening a project, so a batch legitimately sits overnight, and an SLA tighter than the working day would fill the queues with pages nobody is late on.

escalation.$comment: Attempt ceiling for a page that keeps failing. WIRED: tools/tracker/qa-driver.mjs compares it against the ledger's `attempts` on the skip rule, so a page at or over the ceiling is skipped with its last verdict printed and only --force moves it. A pass resets the count to 0, because an attempt count records unresolved trouble and a page that has been fixed must not inherit the ceiling it hit before. In the pipeline this was ported from the counter was incremented and never compared, which let a page be re-judged for ever. tx-driver.mjs must do the same or say why not.

groups.$comment-groups: Four tracked page groups. The key IS the group name IS the sheet basename — config.mjs refuses a registry where they disagree, because a mismatch is what made escalation `group` values unmatchable against work-queue `group` values and left most groups unfilterable in the UI. org/repo are spelled out per entry for readability and asserted against scripts/tracker/paths.js at load. Each sheet is a multi-sheet doc: a `data` master tab plus one tab per target locale.

indexes.$comment: Root home page plus the section index pages. Hand-authored page list in the group sheet — `/` sits outside every index's include: /en/**, so it needs a manual row. Small, high-visibility, own baseline and brief.

meetups.$comment: /en/meetups/**, resolved by PATH PREFIX and never by `template`: 'meetups' is missing from scripts/scripts.js templatedSections, so those pages carry no template metadata at all and a template-keyed sync classifies every one of them as ungrouped.

technical-articles.$comment: /en/articles/**, from /en/query-index.json filtered on path prefix. The largest group, and the one where text expansion bites hardest — code blocks must survive translation byte-identical.

bios.$comment: /en/fragments/bios/**, page list from the /bios.json roster. READ-ONLY coupling: the tracker reads that roster and never writes it — it is owned elsewhere. /en/fragments/** is excluded from the aemdev-en index, so this group has no query-index until a bios index is deployed.
